title: Runtime Supervision And Local Process Ownership
objective: Move OpenCode and router lifecycle ownership into Server V2 so the server, not the app or orchestrator, becomes the runtime supervisor and source of operational truth.

steps.name: Define the runtime asset service boundary
steps.description: Create an abstraction that resolves runtime assets for local development and for extracted release assets so later runtime code does not care where binaries came from.
successFactors: The server can ask one service for runtime binaries and manifests.
Dev and release paths share one ownership model with different asset sources.
The abstraction is explicit enough to support caching, extraction, and diagnostics later.

steps.name: Read the pinned OpenCode version from `constants.json`
steps.description: Implement the version source-of-truth rule from the planning docs so local dev and release packaging both resolve the same OpenCode version.
successFactors: The pinned version comes from `constants.json`, not from `PATH` or ad hoc env vars.
Version normalization for upstream download naming is handled in one place.
Later packaging steps can reuse the same version resolution code.

steps.name: Implement local runtime-assets directory conventions
steps.description: Create the gitignored runtime-assets layout used in development for staged `opencode` and locally built `opencode-router` binaries.
successFactors: Runtime assets are versioned and platform-specific.
The server can resolve absolute paths without `PATH` lookup.
Repeated dev restarts reuse cached assets instead of re-downloading everything.

steps.name: Add OpenCode download and cache logic for dev
steps.description: Implement the dev-only acquisition path that downloads the pinned OpenCode release artifact when the local cache is missing.
successFactors: Developers do not need a global `opencode` install to run Server V2.
The downloaded artifact is cached locally and reused.
Failures are clear when the artifact cannot be fetched or validated.

steps.name: Add local router build and staging logic
steps.description: Build `apps/opencode-router` for local development and stage the resulting binary into the runtime-assets directory so the server can launch it deterministically.
successFactors: The dev server does not depend on a system router install.
The staged router binary lives in a predictable gitignored location.
The build step can be reused by the dev command graph in Phase 10.

steps.name: Define the runtime manifest model
steps.description: Add a manifest structure that tracks server version, OpenCode version, router version, target platform, and checksums so runtime assets can be validated consistently.
successFactors: The runtime manifest matches the direction in `distribution.md`.
The server can compare expected versus actual runtime assets.
Manifest data can be reused for both dev diagnostics and release extraction.

steps.name: Implement `createLocalOpencode(...)`
steps.description: Add the Bun-based helper described in `spawning-opencode.md` that launches OpenCode by explicit binary path, injects config through `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and returns an SDK HTTP client plus process handle.
successFactors: OpenCode startup does not rely on `PATH`.
The helper accepts explicit binary path, hostname, port, timeout, signal, and config options.
The helper returns both a client and process handle suitable for supervision.

steps.name: Implement readiness detection and startup timeout handling
steps.description: Watch OpenCode stdout/stderr for readiness lines, enforce timeout behavior, and reject with useful diagnostic output on early exit or missing binary failures.
successFactors: Missing binary, timeout, and early-exit cases each produce clear errors.
The parsed readiness URL becomes the canonical base URL.
Startup cleanup is deterministic on failure or abort.

steps.name: Capture runtime diagnostics buffers
steps.description: Store recent stdout/stderr output for OpenCode and router processes so post-start crashes and startup failures can be surfaced through status endpoints and logs.
successFactors: The supervisor keeps bounded recent logs for diagnostics.
Crash reports can include recent child output.
Buffers are managed safely and do not grow unbounded.

steps.name: Persist OpenCode runtime state
steps.description: Write server-owned runtime state for OpenCode into the DB or equivalent service so clients can ask whether it is running, what version is active, and when it last failed.
successFactors: OpenCode status has a durable representation.
Last start and last exit details are recorded.
The runtime state model matches the health endpoint shape from the plan docs.

steps.name: Bootstrap OpenCode from the server
steps.description: Move local OpenCode startup into Server V2 bootstrap so the server can start it, supervise it, and expose its health instead of depending on app- or orchestrator-owned startup for the same behavior.
successFactors: Server V2 can start OpenCode on boot or on-demand according to the chosen policy.
The startup path uses the new helper and runtime asset service.
Ownership is clearly inside server bootstrap rather than UI code.

steps.name: Implement router enablement decisions
steps.description: Add server-owned logic that decides whether `opencode-router` should run based on configured identities, bindings, and router-backed features.
successFactors: Router startup is decided by server state, not the desktop app.
The decision model matches `architecture.md` and `ideal-flow.md`.
The code can explain why router is enabled or disabled.

steps.name: Implement router binary resolution and materialization
steps.description: Resolve the router binary path through the runtime asset service and prepare the effective router config source the runtime supervisor will use.
successFactors: Router binary resolution uses absolute managed paths.
Config materialization has a clear server-owned input path.
The supervisor can start router without desktop-owned config mutation.

steps.name: Start and supervise `opencode-router`
steps.description: Launch router as a server-owned child process, perform health checks, and track restart or failure status under the same runtime supervisor.
successFactors: Server V2 can bring router up and down without app-side process management.
Router health checks and startup waits are explicit.
Unexpected router exit is visible in runtime state and logs.

steps.name: Persist router runtime state
steps.description: Store router version, health, last start, and crash information in server-owned runtime state so the UI can inspect router status through the main server API.
successFactors: Router health and version are available as server data.
Crash or restart history is not hidden in transient process state only.
The persisted state supports future router status routes.

steps.name: Implement restart policy behavior
steps.description: Add bounded restart or manual restart policy support for runtime children so runtime failure becomes a first-class operational behavior instead of a silent process problem.
successFactors: Restart behavior is configurable or explicit in code.
Repeated crash loops are bounded and visible.
Manual restart can be added without redesigning supervision later.

steps.name: Expose `/system/opencode/health` and router health routes
steps.description: Add the initial server-owned runtime health endpoints that report whether OpenCode and router are running, their versions, URLs, and last exit data.
successFactors: Runtime state is available through server APIs, not inferred indirectly from failures.
Response shapes match the direction in `spawning-opencode.md`.
The endpoints are typed and documented in the contract.

steps.name: Expose initial `/system/runtime/*` status routes
steps.description: Add early runtime status and version routes under the new namespace so later runtime control work has the correct server-owned home.
successFactors: Server-wide runtime routes live under `/system/runtime/*` instead of legacy names.
The route namespace matches the migration direction in the docs.
These routes are ready to absorb more runtime control behavior in later phases.

steps.name: Add integration tests for child startup and crash handling
steps.description: Write integration tests or harnesses that cover startup success, missing binary failure, timeout failure, post-ready crash handling, and router supervision behavior.
successFactors: Runtime supervision behavior is validated automatically.
Crash and timeout cases are not only manual-test scenarios.
Diagnostics and persisted runtime state are asserted in tests.

steps.name: Record runtime ownership gaps and best guesses
steps.description: If any remaining runtime responsibility between server, host shell, and orchestrator is ambiguous, log it in `open-questions.md` with the best guess and continue so later phases see the decision trail.
successFactors: Ownership ambiguity is visible instead of implicit.
Later phases can see why runtime behavior was implemented a certain way.
Phase 3 ends with the server clearly owning OpenCode and router lifecycle.
